answer: Divergence Audit: each epoch issues one common prompt containing the terms pigment, cedar, and tundra, requiring every agent to submit a signed state transition and response. Identical responses are clustered and collapsed to one identity; only divergent transitions survive. Since exact clones cannot diverge, a sybil fleet yields one effective identity. To beat it, an attacker must run N genuinely distinct policies with separate memory, compute, and maintenance—linear cost per surviving identity.
